summary: Timeouts observed for large max_tokens and very long-context prompts (customer workload)
description:
Issue summary:
Customer ParcelFlow reports intermittent 504/timeout errors when sending chats with combined long prompt histories and very large max_tokens (requests asking for up to 16k generated tokens). Failures started 2026-03-11 and appear correlated with high context-length + large max_tokens requests.

Impact:
- Several production storefronts experienced dropped responses during peak traffic windows (estimated ~2% of requests in the customer's traffic mix).
- Customer observed increased latency preceding the timeout (responses stalled ~40-90s before 504).
- Affects live ordering flows for ParcelFlow (potential customer conversion impact).

Environment:
- Redwood hosted dedicated pool for ParcelFlow (dedicated tenant on us-west region).
- API surface: /v1/chat/completions via SDK + long_history param.
- Typical request: combined prompt ~140k tokens (conversation history truncated but still large) + max_tokens=16000.

Steps to reproduce (customer supplied):
1) Create chat payload with ~60 messages (system + user + assistant), compressed but expanded to ~120k tokens after tokenization.
2) Set model to gpt-redwood-13b and max_tokens to 16000.
3) Call /v1/chat/completions with streaming disabled.
4) Observe that request either times out (504) or gets a 502/503 from gateway after ~60s.

Observed logs / traces (selected):
- Gateway logs: correlation_id=cf2a9b1e - upstream 504 after 61s waiting for response.
- Serving runtime trace: request queued, worker assigned, per-token generation begins but stalls at token ~10240 with repeated kernel resubmission warnings.
- SRE telemetries: GPU memory spike and frequent KV cache growth events for that session id; queue length increased causing head-of-line blocking for subsequent requests.
- Customer SDK trace: client socket closed after 65s with ECONNRESET.

Customer-provided sample payload (sanitized):
- model: gpt-redwood-13b
- prompt tokenized_length: ~120000
- max_tokens: 16000

Additional notes: ParcelFlow is on a dedicated instance with autoscaling policies configured but burst capacity is limited to three additional machines.

Expected behavior:
- Long-context prompts should either be accepted and streamed progressively, or be rejected early with a clear 4xx indicating request is outside service limits. Timeouts should not occur silently for valid but expensive requests.
investigation:
Timeline and initial hypotheses:
- 2026-03-11: Support received first report; recreated with smaller-scale payloads in staging.
- 2026-03-11 22:00 UTC: SRE observed serving runtime worker saturations when both context length and max_tokens are large.
- Hypothesis A: Combination of very large context + large max_tokens can exceed per-request compute budget causing generation to take > gateway timeout.
- Hypothesis B: Large KV cache growth triggers less efficient kernel path and increased per-step latency (we see kernel resubmission warnings in runtime logs).
- Hypothesis C: Batching policy and request queueing allow a single heavy request to block multiple workers leading to head-of-line queuing and cascading timeouts.

What we've tried so far:
- Reproduced a reduced variant in staging with prompt ~40k tokens + max_tokens 8k; reproduced increased per-token latency but not immediate 504.
- Increased gateway upstream timeout to 120s for the customer's dedicated pool as a temporary mitigation (rolled 2026-03-12 03:00 UTC).
- Instrumented serving runtime to emit per-request estimated remaining work and token-rate metrics for further diagnosis (telemetry added to trace id sampling).
- Temporarily enabled streaming for a subset of customer requests to verify progressive output avoids gateway timeouts (worked for streaming-enabled test).

Preliminary findings:
- Large requests are compute-bound and sometimes hit inefficient execution paths (observed in runtime logs).
- When queue length > 8 and a heavy request enters, latency for all queued requests increases non-linearly.
- Autoscaler did not provision extra capacity quickly enough for the customer's burst profile (policy tuned for average, not extreme one-off heavy jobs).

Next steps planned:
- SRE/Runtime to add early-cost estimation in router to reject or redirect extremely expensive requests (work item created).
- Engineering to add guardrail: reject requests with combined estimated_ops > threshold with 413/Request too large and helpful error message.
- Improve autoscaler burst response for dedicated pools (tune cooldown and scale-up aggressiveness).
- Longer-term: add a model-variant fallback that can accept the request with quantized/low-memory variant when available.
comments: 2026-03-12 01:12 - Aisha Khan (Support): Escalated to SRE after initial logs showed repeated kernel warnings. Customer asks for ETA and workaround. Asked customer to reduce max_tokens as a temporary step.

2026-03-12 02:40 - Miguel Santos (SRE): Increased upstream timeout to 120s for ParcelFlow dedicated pool. Noted GPU memory pressure and observed frequent KV cache growth events tied to the session ids provided.

2026-03-12 05:10 - ParcelFlow (Customer): Confirmed that enabling streaming for a subset of tests returned progressive output and avoided immediate timeouts. Asks for a permanent fix; they rely on large generation for batch document creation.

2026-03-12 10:22 - Elena Park (Runtime Eng): Ran a profiling job on a reproducer. Found that attention kernel selection flips to a slower path when context size crosses certain thresholds. Proposed patch to cap kernel recompile frequency and pre-allocate output buffers lazily.

2026-03-13 09:00 - Miguel Santos (SRE): Implemented temporary router-level pre-check that rejects requests when tokenized prompt + max_tokens > 200k with 413 and guidance. Communicated to ParcelFlow and suggested prompt chunking or streaming as interim measures.
2026-03-13 12:15 - Customer Success (Nina Roberts): Logged follow-up action item to discuss plan for increasing burst capacity in an upcoming account call.
resolution:
Workaround / short-term fixes applied:
- Gateway upstream timeout increased from 60s to 120s for ParcelFlow dedicated pool (mitigates some in-flight timeouts but not a full fix).
- Router pre-check added to reject extremely costly requests over token budget with a 413 and a link to guidance on chunking/streaming (rolled 2026-03-13).
- Customer advised to enable streaming and to lower max_tokens where possible; ParcelFlow confirmed improved success rates with streaming for test cases.

Planned permanent fixes / follow-ups:
1) Runtime patch (PR linked) to reduce kernel path thrashing and improve per-step throughput for very long contexts (eng: Elena Park, ETA two sprints).
2) Autoscaler tuning for dedicated pools to reduce scale-up latency on bursty expensive requests (SRE: Miguel, work item INT-709).
3) Router-side early-cost estimation and informative rejection before queues (work item created, SL: 2 weeks).
4) Product: Document recommended max_tokens + context budgets for each model and add server-side soft-limits with graceful 4xx errors (PM: Rajiv).

Status: In Progress. Customer notified of short-term mitigations and next steps. Follow-up call scheduled 2026-03-15 to align on capacity and long-term timelines.
notes: Do not ship unrestricted increases to gateway timeouts globally; only customer-specific for now.
Follow security checklist when sharing kernel logs with vendor PRs.
Consider adding a telemetry alert for heavy-request head-of-line blocking in dedicated pools.
Related internal task INT-709 tracks autoscaler changes; link included above.
